content: Acetaminophen oral solution is a medication classified as an analgesic and antipyretic, meaning it is used to relieve pain and reduce fever. It is approved by the FDA for the temporary relief of minor aches and pains associated with conditions such as headaches, muscle aches, backaches, minor arthritis pain, the common cold, toothaches, and premenstrual or menstrual cramps. It is also used to temporarily reduce fever. Common side effects of acetaminophen oral solution include itching (pruritus), constipation, nausea, vomiting, headache, agitation, insomnia, and atelectasis (partial lung collapse). The maximum daily dose for adults is six doses within a 24-hour period, and for children, it is five doses within the same timeframe. Exceeding these limits can result in severe liver damage. Adults who consume three or more alcoholic beverages daily are at an increased risk of liver damage when using this product. This medication should not be used in combination with other drugs containing acetaminophen, whether prescription or over-the-counter, as this increases the risk of overdose. Additionally, individuals allergic to acetaminophen or any of the inactive ingredients in the product should avoid its use. Patients with liver disease should consult a doctor before using this medication. Those taking the blood-thinning medication warfarin should also seek medical advice before use, as acetaminophen may interact with this drug. If pain worsens or persists for more than 10 days in adults, or more than 5 days in children under 12, medical attention should be sought. Similarly, if fever worsens or lasts more than 3 days, or if new symptoms such as redness, swelling, or other concerning signs develop, a doctor should be consulted promptly. These symptoms could indicate a more serious underlying condition. In cases of overdose, immediate medical attention is critical, even if no symptoms are initially apparent. Overdose can lead to severe liver damage. Contact a Poison Control Center at 1-800-222-1222 or seek emergency medical help immediately. Pregnant or breastfeeding individuals should consult a healthcare professional before using acetaminophen oral solution. There is no specific FDA guidance on its use during labor and delivery, in geriatric patients, or in individuals with renal or hepatic impairment. Similarly, there is no specific guidance on its use in immunocompromised patients, or in relation to gender or racial populations. The medication is administered orally and should be stored at a temperature of 20° to 25°C (68° to 77°F). It is supplied as a red, cherry-flavored solution in various unit dose cup sizes. The sodium content is 2 mg per 5 mL. The product should be kept tightly closed and protected from light. Patients should avoid consuming alcohol while taking this medication, as the interaction between alcohol and acetaminophen has not been fully established. It is important to discuss alcohol use with a healthcare provider when using this medication. For any serious side effects or concerns, patients can report them by calling 1-800-845-8210.
